source_semantics.question: How can modular Sources, Filters and Sinks be substituted in an electrophysiology acquisition/display chain?
source_semantics.main_path: Acquisition hardware → Rhythm FPGA software Source → Bandpass Filter → LFP Viewer visualization Sink.
source_semantics.grouping_and_layout: Left-to-right dataflow makes the illustrated processing order visible. Alternative cards grouped by Source/Filter/Sink role and curved interchangeability arcs distinguish replaceable implementations from the active example chain.
boundaries: Physical acquisition hardware is distinct from the Rhythm FPGA software Source (p. 5 Sources/Table 1; pp. 7–8 hardware).
Pre-bandpass Source output may already be filtered/amplified in the hardware; do not call it wholly raw/unprocessed (p. 7).
LFP Viewer displays continuous signals and does not imply low-frequency-only content; hardware/software filters affect displayed content (p. 4).
Record Engines/File Sources describe disk writing/loading separately; Figure 3 gives no recording branch/location (p. 6).
Interchangeability arcs do not mean feedback. Optional source threads and generic split/merge descriptions do not establish asynchronous scheduling for this displayed chain (pp. 3–6).
source_semantics.omitted_or_unknown: Exact runtime buffers/scheduling, recorder enablement/location, closed-loop feedback path for this chain, numerical filter/latency/performance consequences, and current software behavior.
